title: Can one check bit catch every error?
hook: A receiver checks one extra bit. Two bits flip in transit. What does the check say?

doesNotKnow: how a parity check bit is chosen and tested
that parity misses any even number of flipped bits

misconception: A check bit catches any corruption of the message.
objective: The learner can explain that each bit flip switches the count of 1s between even and odd, so an even-parity check catches one (or any odd number of) flips and passes two (or any even number), wherever they are.

claims.text: An even-parity check bit is chosen so that the count of 1s, check bit included, is even; the receiver passes the message if the count it gets is even.
claims.source: Definition of even parity: Tanenbaum and Wetherall, Computer Networks, 5th ed., 3.2.2 'Error-detecting codes'. Demo.tsx CHECK and passes().

claims.text: Every bit flip changes the count of 1s by one, switching it between even and odd, so a single flip is always caught.
claims.source: A flip turns a 0 into 1 (+1) or a 1 into 0 (-1); either changes the parity of the count.

claims.text: Two flips anywhere in the message, check bit included, leave the count even again, so the check passes on a wrong message; in general parity catches any odd number of flips and misses any even number.
claims.source: k flips change the count by k changes of parity; parity is restored iff k is even. The stage lets the learner test 1 to 8 flips on the message 1011010 + check bit 0. · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Exhaustively checked all 255 non-empty flip patterns of the 8 bits: pass iff the flip count is even.

claims.text: In the stage's message the seven data bits hold four 1s, so the even-parity check bit is 0; the receiver passes a message when the count of 1s it gets is even. One check bit cannot guard a message against noise that flips several bits.
claims.source: DATA = 1,0,1,1,0,1,0 in Demo.tsx: four 1s, check = 4 mod 2 = 0. Last clause follows from the claim that two flips pass the check.

recall.question: A byte with an even-parity bit arrives and the check passes. What do you know?
options: An even number of bits flipped, possibly zero
recall.why: Each flip switches the count of 1s between even and odd, so the check passes after 0, 2, 4 ... flips. A pass only rules out an odd number of flips.
